answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is earned back only through verified useful work, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Think of reputation as a garden: trust grows gradually and visibly, while a fake identity is like shale - layered thin and crumbling under scrutiny. Any fable of free, instant trust is false; attackers must pay real time and capital for each identity, and slashing the deposit on detected fraud makes mass fakery unprofitable while honest agents recover their stake.
